literature.headline_zh: 发热伴血小板减少综合征病毒本期文献呈现多方向研究进展
literature.lead_zh: 本期发热伴血小板减少综合征病毒研究集中呈现以下进展。
key_findings_zh: 一些康复的猫表现出高PRNT 80滴度,且在感染后早期被动给予高滴度恢复期猫血清可保护SFTSV感染的小鼠。在感染后第2或第3天给予单次剂量可完全保护小鼠,而感染后第4天给予则导致40%的存活率。 [10.1016/j.vetmic.2026.111264]
BmKDfsin3在A549细胞中浓度依赖性地抑制了SFTSV和HSV-1的复制,主要作用于病毒生命周期的进入后阶段。它还抑制了p38的激活,并增强了I型和III型干扰素信号通路。 [10.1128/spectrum.01788-26]
分解结果以每年病例数和每100基线病例数的形式呈现,同时包括多种情景分析,如固定率标准化情景、八个地区四个因素分解、性别特异性分析以及补充泊松区间。 [10.17605/osf.io/fd95u]
经过这些多模式干预后,患者顺利脱离机械通气并成功拔管。其临床指标、病毒载量和炎症标志物随着器官功能的恢复而逐渐下降,最终实现成功出院。 [10.21203/rs.3.rs-10930938/v1]
现有数据表明,SFTSV的暴露和感染发生在广泛的动物宿主中,支持多宿主生态框架,而非简单的单一宿主解释。 [10.71150/jm.2608006]
literature.trend_or_risk_zh: 本期研究方向以入选文献实际覆盖的临床、流行病学、宿主生态、诊断或分子监测主题为准。
literature.headline_en: Recent Severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome virus literature
literature.lead_en: This reporting window highlights the following research developments.
key_findings_en: Some SFTS-recovered cats exhibited high PRNT 80 titers, and passive administration of high-titer convalescent cat serum early after infection protected SFTSV-infected mice, with a single dose given at 2 or 3 days post-infection completely protecting mice, whereas treatment at 4 days post-infection resulted in 40% survival. [10.1016/j.vetmic.2026.111264]

BmKDfsin3 concentration-dependently inhibited SFTSV and HSV-1 replication in A549 cells, primarily targeting the post-entry stage of the viral life cycle. It also suppressed p38 activation and enhanced type I and III interferon signaling pathways. [10.1128/spectrum.01788-26]

The decomposition results are presented in cases per year and per 100 baseline cases, alongside various scenarios including a fixed-rate standardised scenario, an eight-region four-factor decomposition, sex-specific analyses, and a supplementary Poisson interval. [10.17605/osf.io/fd95u]

Following these multimodal interventions, the patient was smoothly weaned from mechanical ventilation and successfully extubated. His clinical indicators, viral load and inflammatory markers progressively declined alongside the recovery of organ function, ultimately resulting in a successful discharge. [10.21203/rs.3.rs-10930938/v1]

Available data indicate that SFTSV exposure and infection occur across a broad range of animal hosts, supporting a multi-host ecological framework rather than a simple single-reservoir interpretation. [10.71150/jm.2608006]

papers.title: High-titer convalescent serum from cats recovered from severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome protects SFTSV-infected mice.
papers.abstract: Severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome (SFTS) is an emerging tick-borne zoonosis caused by severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome virus (SFTSV) and is associated with high case-fatality rates in humans and cats. No vaccines or antiviral drugs are currently available for the prevention or treatment of feline SFTS. We hypothesized that some cats that recover from naturally acquired SFTS develop high neutralizing antibody titers and may serve as a source of convalescent serum for passive immunotherapy. We measured 80% plaque-reduction neutralization test (PRNT 80 ) titers in convalescent sera from six human SFTS survivors and 14 cats that had recovered from naturally acquired SFTS, and then evaluated the therapeutic efficacy of convalescent cat serum in SFTSV-infected, interferon receptor-deficient AG129 mice. Some SFTS-recovered cats exhibited high PRNT 80 titers. Passive administration of high-titer convalescent cat serum early after infection protected SFTSV-infected mice. A single dose given at 2 or 3 days post-infection completely protected mice, whereas treatment at 4 days post-infection resulted in 40% survival. In the repeated-dose experiment, early treatment was associated with lower blood viral RNA levels than controls at 6 dpi, and surviving mice also showed low viral RNA levels at 13 dpi. Sera from three additional SFTS-recovered cats also improved survival. Collectively, these findings indicate that some SFTS-recovered cats can develop high neutralizing antibody titers and that their sera can exert therapeutic effects in an SFTSV-infected mouse model, supporting further evaluation of passive immunotherapy as a treatment strategy for feline SFTS.

We measured 80% plaque-reduction neutralization test (PRNT 80 ) titers in convalescent sera from six human SFTS survivors and 14 cats that had recovered from naturally acquired SFTS, and then evaluated the therapeutic efficacy of convalescent cat serum in SFTSV-infected, interferon receptor-deficient AG129 mice. Some SFTS-recovered cats exhibited high PRNT 80 titers. Passive administration of high-titer convalescent cat serum early after infection protected SFTSV-infected mice. A single dose given at 2 or 3 days post-infection completely protected mice, whereas treatment at 4 days post-infection resulted in 40% survival. In the repeated-dose experiment, early treatment was associated with lower blood viral RNA levels than controls at 6 dpi, and surviving mice also showed low viral RNA levels at 13 dpi. Sera from three additional SFTS-recovered cats also improved survival. Collectively, these findings indicate that some SFTS-recovered cats can develop high neutralizing antibody titers and that their sera can exert therapeutic effects in an SFTSV-infected mouse model, supporting further evaluation of passive immunotherapy as a treatment strategy for feline SFTS.
papers.abstract_zh: 发热伴血小板减少综合征(发热伴血小板减少综合征)是一种由发热伴血小板减少综合征病毒(SFTSV)引起的新兴疾病,与人类和猫的高死亡率相关。目前尚无抗病毒药物或治疗药物可用于预防或治疗猫的发热伴血小板减少综合征。我们假设一些从自然感染中康复的猫会发展出高中和抗体滴度,可能作为被动免疫治疗的恢复期血清来源。我们测量了六名人类发热伴血小板减少综合征康复者的恢复期血清以及14只自然感染后康复的猫的恢复期血清中80%斑块减少中和试验(PRNT 80)滴度,并评估了这些恢复期猫血清在SFTSV感染、干扰素受体缺陷的AG129小鼠中的治疗效果。一些康复的猫表现出高PRNT 80滴度。在感染后早期被动给予高滴度恢复期猫血清可保护SFTSV感染的小鼠。在感染后第2或第3天给予单次剂量可完全保护小鼠,而感染后第4天给予则导致40%的存活率。在重复剂量实验中,早期治疗与对照组相比,在感染后第6天表现出更低的血液病毒RNA水平,存活的小鼠在感染后第13天也显示出较低的病毒RNA水平。另外三只康复猫的血清也改善了存活率。总体而言,这些发现表明一些康复的猫可以发展出高中和抗体滴度,其血清在SFTSV感染的小鼠模型中具有治疗效果,支持进一步评估被动免疫治疗作为猫发热伴血小板减少综合征的治疗策略。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在通过调查从发热伴血小板减少综合征康复的猫的恢复期血清是否可用于被动免疫治疗,解决目前尚无抗病毒药物或治疗药物用于预防或治疗猫发热伴血小板减少综合征的问题。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究涉及测量六名人类发热伴血小板减少综合征康复者的恢复期血清以及14只自然感染后康复的猫的恢复期血清中的中和抗体滴度,并评估这些血清在SFTSV感染、干扰素受体缺陷的AG129小鼠中的治疗效果。
analysis_zh.methods: 研究人员使用80%斑块减少中和试验(PRNT 80)测量中和抗体滴度,并评估恢复期猫血清在SFTSV感染小鼠中的治疗效果。
analysis_zh.main_results: 一些康复的猫表现出高PRNT 80滴度,且在感染后早期被动给予高滴度恢复期猫血清可保护SFTSV感染的小鼠。在感染后第2或第3天给予单次剂量可完全保护小鼠,而感染后第4天给予则导致40%的存活率。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 这些发现表明一些康复的猫可以发展出高中和抗体滴度,其血清在SFTSV感染的小鼠模型中具有治疗效果,支持进一步评估被动免疫治疗作为猫发热伴血小板减少综合征的治疗策略。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些结果表明恢复期猫血清可用于被动免疫治疗以治疗猫发热伴血小板减少综合征,这可能对开发该疾病的治疗策略具有重要意义。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究的局限性在于样本量较小以及使用了小鼠模型,这可能无法完全反映猫中该疾病的复杂性。由于这些限制,证据强度中等。

papers.title: Demographic decomposition of changes in notifications of Japanese spotted fever, severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome, and scrub typhus in Japan, 2014-2016 versus 2022-2024
papers.abstract: Notifications of several tick- and mite-borne infections in Japan have risen, and an increasing share of patients are aged 70 and over. Both the growth of the older population and change in age-specific notification rates can produce that pattern, while national and local population decline works in the opposite direction. This study decomposes the change in average annual notifications between 2014-2016 and 2022-2024 into three additive contributions - national population size, age composition across the published age classes, and age-class-specific notification rates - for Japanese spotted fever, severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome and scrub typhus, using the same population series, comparison periods and decomposition rule for all three. The decomposition averages over all permutations of the factors (Shapley-Shorrocks), so no separate interaction term remains and the result does not depend on substitution order. Contributions are reported in cases per year and per 100 baseline cases, alongside a fixed-rate standardised scenario, an eight-region four-factor decomposition, sex-specific analyses, scenario analyses for composition within the open 70-and-over class, a supplementary Poisson interval and a leave-one-year-out range. Only published aggregate statistics are used. The contributions are standardisation quantities, not causal effects, preventable case counts or infection counts, and the protocol fixes in advance how they may and may not be described. Scrub typhus is included as a disease with a different notification trend and is explicitly not a negative control. This registration is made before bulk retrieval of the source tables for all years; the information already viewed is enumerated rather than claiming that no data have been seen.

papers.title: Clinical Management Strategy for a Severe Case of Novel Bunyavirus Infection Complicated by Invasive Aspergillosis in an Elderly Patient
papers.abstract: Abstract Background Severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome (SFTS) is an acute infectious disease caused by severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome virus (SFTSV, also known as Dabie bandavirus), representing an emerging tick-borne disease. Complications such as encephalopathy and secondary invasive fungal infections significantly increase the mortality rate of this disease, for which no specific antiviral therapeutics are currently approved. Case Report: A 70-year-old male patient presented with persistent fever, thrombocytopenia and bleeding tendencies following a tick bite. His condition deteriorated rapidly, characterized by convulsions, cognitive impairment and multiple organ dysfunction, leading to a confirmed diagnosis of severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome complicated by secondary invasive invasive aspergillosis. The patient’s life was successfully saved through a comprehensive clinical regimen, including early antiviral therapy with favipiravir, broad-spectrum anti-infective treatment, targeted antifungal therapy against Aspergillus with voriconazole, anti-inflammatory intervention with low-dose intravenous methylprednisolone, immune modulation using intravenous immunoglobulin, multiple sessions of therapeutic plasma exchange, liver protection, acid suppression, hemostasis and precise anticoagulation guided by dynamic risk assessments of hemorrhage and thrombosis. Following these multimodal interventions, the patient was smoothly weaned from mechanical ventilation and successfully extubated. His clinical indicators, viral load and inflammatory markers progressively declined alongside the recovery of organ function, ultimately resulting in a successful discharge. Conclusion This rare case of severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome complicated by invasive aspergillosis highlights two key priorities in the management of critically ill older patients: close monitoring for neurological complications and secondary fungal infections, together with a multidimensional therapeutic approach incorporating antiviral therapy, plasma exchange for immunomodulation and targeted antifungal treatment.

analysis.summary_en: This case report describes a 70-year-old male patient with severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome (SFTS) complicated by invasive aspergillosis. The patient presented with persistent fever, thrombocytopenia, and bleeding tendencies following a tick bite, and his condition rapidly deteriorated with convulsions, cognitive impairment, and multiple organ dysfunction. The study highlights the importance of close monitoring for neurological complications and secondary fungal infections in elderly patients with SFTS. A comprehensive clinical regimen, including early antiviral therapy with favipiravir, broad-spectrum anti-infective treatment, targeted antifungal therapy with voriconazole, anti-inflammatory intervention with low-dose intravenous methylprednisolone, immune modulation using intravenous immunoglobulin, therapeutic plasma exchange, liver protection, acid suppression, hemostasis, and precise anticoagulation guided by dynamic risk assessments, was employed. The patient was successfully extubated and discharged after his clinical indicators, viral load, and inflammatory markers declined alongside recovery of organ function. The case underscores the need for a multidimensional therapeutic approach in managing severe SFTS, particularly in older patients at risk for secondary fungal infections. The study is a single case report and does not provide statistical or comparative data, limiting its generalizability.

papers.title_zh: 老年患者新型布尼亚病毒感染合并侵袭性曲霉病的临床管理策略
papers.source_body_en: Abstract Background Severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome (SFTS) is an acute infectious disease caused by severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome virus (SFTSV, also known as Dabie bandavirus), representing an emerging tick-borne disease. Complications such as encephalopathy and secondary invasive fungal infections significantly increase the mortality rate of this disease, for which no specific antiviral therapeutics are currently approved. Case Report: A 70-year-old male patient presented with persistent fever, thrombocytopenia and bleeding tendencies following a tick bite. His condition deteriorated rapidly, characterized by convulsions, cognitive impairment and multiple organ dysfunction, leading to a confirmed diagnosis of severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome complicated by secondary invasive invasive aspergillosis. The patient’s life was successfully saved through a comprehensive clinical regimen, including early antiviral therapy with favipiravir, broad-spectrum anti-infective treatment, targeted antifungal therapy against Aspergillus with voriconazole, anti-inflammatory intervention with low-dose intravenous methylprednisolone, immune modulation using intravenous immunoglobulin, multiple sessions of therapeutic plasma exchange, liver protection, acid suppression, hemostasis and precise anticoagulation guided by dynamic risk assessments of hemorrhage and thrombosis. Following these multimodal interventions, the patient was smoothly weaned from mechanical ventilation and successfully extubated. His clinical indicators, viral load and inflammatory markers progressively declined alongside the recovery of organ function, ultimately resulting in a successful discharge. Conclusion This rare case of severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome complicated by invasive aspergillosis highlights two key priorities in the management of critically ill older patients: close monitoring for neurological complications and secondary fungal infections, together with a multidimensional therapeutic approach incorporating antiviral therapy, plasma exchange for immunomodulation and targeted antifungal treatment.
papers.abstract_zh: 摘要 背景 发热伴血小板减少综合征(发热伴血小板减少综合征)是由发热伴血小板减少综合征病毒(SFTSV,也称为大别山布尼亚病毒)引起的急性传染病,代表一种新兴的人兽共患病。脑病和继发性侵袭性真菌感染等并发症显著增加了该病的死亡率,目前尚无针对该病的特异性治疗药物。病例:一名70岁男性患者因蜱咬后出现持续发热、血小板减少和出血倾向。其病情迅速恶化,表现为抽搐、认知功能障碍和多器官功能障碍,最终确诊为发热伴血小板减少综合征合并继发性侵袭性曲霉病。通过综合临床治疗方案,包括早期使用favipiravir进行抗病毒治疗、广谱抗感染治疗、针对曲霉菌的伏立康唑靶向抗真菌治疗、低剂量静脉甲基强的松龙抗炎干预、静脉免疫球蛋白免疫调节、多次治疗性血浆置换、保肝、抑酸、止血以及基于出血和血栓动态风险评估的精准抗凝治疗,患者生命得以成功挽救。经过这些多模式干预后,患者顺利脱离机械通气并成功拔管。其临床指标、病毒载量和炎症标志物随着器官功能的恢复而逐渐下降,最终实现成功出院。结论 这一罕见的发热伴血小板减少综合征合并侵袭性曲霉病病例突出了对重症老年患者管理的两个关键优先事项:密切监测神经系统并发症和继发性真菌感染,以及采用多维治疗策略,包括抗病毒治疗、血浆置换用于免疫调节和针对曲霉菌的靶向抗真菌治疗。

papers.title: Inhibitory activity and mechanism of a scorpion-derived peptide BmKDfsin3 against SFTSV and HSV-1
papers.abstract: UNLABELLED: Antiviral peptides, as an important source of antiviral drugs, will have significant application value and potential in the field of viral prevention and treatment. Therefore, it is of great significance to discover broad-spectrum, highly efficient, and low-toxicity antiviral peptides. Here, we found that the scorpion venom peptide BmKDfsin3 not only concentration-dependently inhibited the replication of severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome virus (SFTSV) but also suppressed the replication of herpes simplex virus type 1 (HSV-1) in A549 cells. The results of antiviral phase assays showed that BmKDfsin3 mainly inhibited the post-entry stage of the life cycle of these two viruses. Mechanistically, BmKDfsin3 effectively suppressed the activation of p38 induced by SFTSV and HSV-1 infections. Furthermore, using poly(I:C) as a viral mimic, we found that BmKDfsin3 enhanced type I and III interferon signaling pathways by activating the transcription factors p52 and IRF3. Importantly, BmKDfsin3 exhibited good biosafety, including low cytotoxicity, hemolytic activity, and mouse toxicity. Overall, BmKDfsin3 was revealed to be a natural bioactive peptide with good biological safety, potent antiviral activity, and a broad antiviral spectrum. IMPORTANCE: The scorpion venom peptide BmKDfsin3 mediates antiviral activity through a dual mechanism: it limits viral replication by inhibiting the exploitation of host p38 signaling by SFTSV and HSV-1, and it promotes host immune responses by activating transcription factors p52 and IRF3 to enhance type I and III interferon (IFN) signaling. This synergy between "inhibiting virus-dependent pathway" and "activating host immunity" confers potent, broad-spectrum antiviral activity upon BmKDfsin3, resulting in significant dose-dependent inhibition against phylogenetically distinct RNA (SFTSV) and DNA (HSV-1) viruses. Importantly, the peptide exhibits minimal cytotoxicity, hemolytic activity, and in vivo toxicity. This study provides new insights into how a single-peptide molecule achieves efficient, broad-spectrum antiviral activity by concurrently targeting virus-dependent and host immune pathways, highlighting the therapeutic potential of antiviral peptides in broad-spectrum drug design.

The study design involved in vitro experiments using A549 cells to assess the peptide's effects on viral replication. Results showed that BmKDfsin3 concentration-dependently inhibited SFTSV and HSV-1 replication, primarily targeting the post-entry stage of their life cycles. Mechanistically, the peptide suppressed p38 activation and enhanced interferon signaling by activating p52 and IRF3. The findings suggest a dual mechanism of action, offering new insights into antiviral peptide design. The study's significance lies in its potential to inform the development of effective antiviral therapies. However, the evidence is limited to in vitro results, and further in vivo studies are necessary to validate these findings.

papers.abstract_zh: 未标注:抗病毒药物肽作为重要的抗病毒药物药物来源,在病毒预防和治疗领域具有显著的应用价值和潜力。因此,发现具有广谱、高效、低毒性的抗病毒药物肽具有重要意义。本研究发现,蝎毒肽BmKDfsin3不仅浓度依赖性地抑制了发热伴血小板减少综合征病毒(SFTSV)的复制,还抑制了单纯疱疹病毒1型(HSV-1)在A549细胞中的复制。抗病毒药物阶段试验的结果显示,BmKDfsin3主要抑制这两种病毒生命周期的进入后阶段。从机制上看,BmKDfsin3有效抑制了SFTSV和HSV-1感染诱导的p38激活。此外,使用聚(I:C)作为病毒模拟物,我们发现BmKDfsin3通过激活转录因子p52和IRF3,增强了I型和III型干扰素信号通路。重要的是,BmKDfsin3表现出良好的生物安全性,包括低细胞毒性、溶血活性和小鼠毒性。总体而言,BmKDfsin3被揭示为一种具有良好生物安全性、强效抗病毒药物活性和广谱抗病毒药物作用的天然生物活性肽。重要性:蝎毒肽BmKDfsin3通过双重机制介导抗病毒药物活性:一方面,它通过抑制SFTSV和HSV-1对宿主 p38信号通路的利用来限制病毒复制;另一方面,它通过激活转录因子p52和IRF3来增强I型和III型干扰素(IFN)信号通路,从而促进宿主 免疫应答。这种"抑制病毒依赖性通路"与"激活宿主免疫"之间的协同作用赋予BmKDfsin3强效、广谱的抗病毒药物活性,导致对系统发育上不同的RNA(SFTSV)和DNA(HSV-1)病毒具有显著的剂量依赖性抑制作用。重要的是,该肽表现出极低的细胞毒性、溶血活性和体内毒性。本研究提供了新的见解,说明单个肽分子如何通过同时靶向病毒依赖性和宿主免疫通路,实现高效、广谱的抗病毒药物活性,突显了抗病毒药物肽在广谱药物设计中的治疗潜力。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在探讨从蝎子中分离的肽对SFTSV和HSV-1的抗病毒药物潜力,以应对病毒预防和治疗领域对广谱、低毒性的抗病毒药物制剂的需求。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究在实验室环境下,考察了蝎毒肽BmKDfsin3对SFTSV和HSV-1在A549细胞中的抑制活性,重点关注病毒复制的抑制。
analysis_zh.methods: 进行了抗病毒药物阶段试验,以评估BmKDfsin3对病毒复制阶段的影响,并通过检测p38和转录因子p52、IRF3的激活情况,以了解其作用机制。
analysis_zh.main_results: BmKDfsin3在A549细胞中浓度依赖性地抑制了SFTSV和HSV-1的复制,主要作用于病毒生命周期的进入后阶段。它还抑制了p38的激活,并增强了I型和III型干扰素信号通路。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果表明,BmKDfsin3通过双重机制起作用,既抑制病毒复制,又促进宿主 免疫应答,这为广谱抗病毒药物活性提供了一种新颖的策略。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些结果表明,BmKDfsin3可能是开发针对RNA和DNA病毒(包括SFTSV和HSV-1)的广谱抗病毒药物疗法的有前景候选物。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究仅限于体外实验,基于直接观察,抗病毒药物活性的证据较强,但需要体内验证以确认其治疗潜力。

papers.title: Epidemiology and spillover risk of SFTSV in animals across East Asia
papers.abstract: Severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome (SFTS) is an emerging tick‐borne zoonosis in East Asia, yet the contribution of animals to virus maintenance and spillover remains incompletely characterized. This review synthesizes current evidence of SFTS virus (SFTSV) infection across domestic livestock, companion animals, wildlife, and captive species, focusing on host range, geographic distribution, diagnostics, and reports of viral RNA and virus isolation. Available data indicate that SFTSV exposure and infection occur across a broad range of animal hosts, supporting a multi-host ecological framework rather than a simple single-reservoir interpretation. Domestic ruminants frequently exhibit high seroprevalence and may function as sentinels of enzootic activity, while occasional virus isolation from cattle demonstrates that viable virus can be recovered from naturally infected livestock, although this does not establish reservoir or amplification competence. Companion animals are considered a potential interface for interspecies transmission, as some studies have documented severe clinical disease, high viral loads, and cat-associated human transmission events supported by varying levels of epidemiological and genomic evidence. Studies in wildlife further document exposure and natural infection across diverse taxa, although their specific roles in viral maintenance remain unresolved. Interpretation of these findings depends heavily on the diagnostic modality: serology primarily indicates prior exposure, RNA detection supports current or recent infection, and virus isolation demonstrates that viable virus was present in the sampled material. Integrating animal infection data within an ecological framework reveals major knowledge gaps related to reservoir competence, infectious shedding, phylogenetic connections among animal, tick, and human cases, and implications for prevention. The review underscores the need for One Health surveillance that incorporates clinical data from companion animals and applies evidence‐based interpretation to improve recognition of animal–human interfaces associated with potential spillover risk.

source_records.abstract: Severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome (SFTS) is an emerging tick‐borne zoonosis in East Asia, yet the contribution of animals to virus maintenance and spillover remains incompletely characterized. This review synthesizes current evidence of SFTS virus (SFTSV) infection across domestic livestock, companion animals, wildlife, and captive species, focusing on host range, geographic distribution, diagnostics, and reports of viral RNA and virus isolation. Available data indicate that SFTSV exposure and infection occur across a broad range of animal hosts, supporting a multi-host ecological framework rather than a simple single-reservoir interpretation. Domestic ruminants frequently exhibit high seroprevalence and may function as sentinels of enzootic activity, while occasional virus isolation from cattle demonstrates that viable virus can be recovered from naturally infected livestock, although this does not establish reservoir or amplification competence. Companion animals are considered a potential interface for interspecies transmission, as some studies have documented severe clinical disease, high viral loads, and cat-associated human transmission events supported by varying levels of epidemiological and genomic evidence. Studies in wildlife further document exposure and natural infection across diverse taxa, although their specific roles in viral maintenance remain unresolved. Interpretation of these findings depends heavily on the diagnostic modality: serology primarily indicates prior exposure, RNA detection supports current or recent infection, and virus isolation demonstrates that viable virus was present in the sampled material. Integrating animal infection data within an ecological framework reveals major knowledge gaps related to reservoir competence, infectious shedding, phylogenetic connections among animal, tick, and human cases, and implications for prevention. The review underscores the need for One Health surveillance that incorporates clinical data from companion animals and applies evidence‐based interpretation to improve recognition of animal–human interfaces associated with potential spillover risk.

analysis.summary_en: This review explores the epidemiology and spillover risk of Severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome virus (SFTSV) in animals across East Asia. The study focuses on the host range, geographic distribution, and diagnostic methods for SFTSV infection in domestic livestock, companion animals, wildlife, and captive species. The findings suggest that SFTSV has a broad range of animal hosts, supporting a multi-host ecological framework rather than a single-reservoir model. While domestic ruminants show high seroprevalence and may act as sentinels for enzootic activity, the role of these animals in viral maintenance and amplification remains unclear. The review highlights the importance of integrating animal infection data into an ecological framework and emphasizes the need for One Health surveillance to better understand and mitigate spillover risks from animal to human populations.

papers.abstract_zh: 发热伴血小板减少综合征(发热伴血小板减少综合征)是一种在东亚地区新兴的蜱媒病毒,然而动物在病毒维持和传播中的作用仍不完全明确。本综述总结了当前关于SFTSV感染在家畜、宠物、野生动物和圈养物种中的证据,重点分析了其宿主范围、地理分布、诊断方法以及病毒RNA检测和病毒分离的报告。现有数据表明,SFTSV的暴露和感染发生在广泛的动物宿主中,支持多宿主生态框架,而非简单的单一宿主解释。家畜(如反刍动物)经常表现出高感染率,可能作为流行病活动的哨兵;偶尔从牛中分离到病毒表明,自然感染的家畜中可以分离出活性病毒,但这一点并不能证明其传播能力或增殖能力。宠物被认为是跨物种传播的潜在接口,因为一些研究记录了严重的临床症状、高病毒载量以及由不同水平的流行病学和基因组证据支持的猫源性人类感染事件。野生动物的研究进一步表明,不同物种中均存在暴露和自然感染,但它们在病毒维持中的具体作用仍未明确。这些发现的解释高度依赖于诊断方法:血清学检测主要表明既往暴露,RNA检测支持当前或近期感染,而病毒分离则表明采样材料中存在活性病毒。将动物感染数据整合到生态框架中,揭示了关于传播能力、传染性排泄、动物、蜱和人类病例之间的系统发育联系以及对预防措施的影响等方面的主要知识空白。综述强调了需要一种结合宠物临床数据的One Health监测策略,并采用基于证据的解释方法,以提高对与潜在传播风险相关的动物-人类接口的认识。

papers.full_text: Severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome (SFTS), caused by Dabie bandavirus, is associated with high mortality among intensive care unit (ICU) patients; however, the integrated proteomic–metabolomic mechanisms underlying fatal outcomes remain poorly characterized. This prospective cohort study enrolled 68 patients with SFTS, who were admitted to the ICU and classified them as survivors (n = 33) or non-survivors (n = 35) according to their 28-day clinical outcomes. Untargeted metabolomic profiling using ultra-high-performance liquid chromatography–tandem mass spectrometry and quantitative proteomic profiling using data-independent acquisition mass spectrometry were performed on plasma samples collected at ICU admission. Multivariable analysis, pathway enrichment analysis, correlation analysis, and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis were used to identify potential prognostic biomarkers and characterize molecular associations. Non-survivors exhibited more severe multi-organ injury and systemic inflammation. Metabolomic profiling revealed marked disruption of tryptophan metabolism: L-tryptophan levels were decreased, whereas kynurenine and its downstream metabolites (kynurenic acid [KA], 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid [3-HAA], xanthurenic acid [XA], and 5-hydroxyindolepyruvate [5-HIP]) were increased, suggesting activation of the kynurenine pathway. The four core tryptophan metabolites yielded a combined area under the curve (AUC) of 0.934 for predicting 28-day mortality and were correlated with indicators of renal function and coagulation. Proteomic profiling identified 200 differentially expressed proteins: proteins upregulated in survivors were enriched in the proteasome pathway, whereas those upregulated in non-survivors were enriched in the IL-17 pathway and other inflammatory and immune pathways. Integrated analysis revealed that the four tryptophan metabolites were associated with 20 differentially expressed proteins, six of which showed robust associations within outcome subgroups. Collectively, tryptophan metabolic disturbances coupled with inflammatory proteomic features may characterize fatal severe SFTS, and the identified metabolite–protein signatures may serve as promising prognostic biomarkers and potential therapeutic targets in critically ill patients. 2Materials and methods2.1Study design and participantsThis prospective cohort study included patients with severe SFTS who were admitted to the ICU between July 2019 and October 2023. According to their 28-day clinical outcomes, patients were divided into survivor (n = 33) and non-survivor (n = 35) groups. All specimens were collected in the Department of Critical Care Medicine, Yantai Qishan Hospital. The study was approved by the Ethics Review Committee of Yantai Qishan Hospital (approval no. 202503). The participants were informed about the research and its potential risks and provided written informed consent in accordance with the Declaration of Helsinki. The inclusion criteria (11) were as follows: (1) detection of novel bunyavirus nucleic acids in blood samples, confirmed by reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR) in the laboratory, and (2) fulfillment of the criteria for severe and critical disease classification outlined in the Consensus on Diagnosis and Treatment of Severe Fever with Thrombocytopenia Syndrome (2022 Edition). The exclusion criteria were as follows: (1) clinically suspected severe SFTS with an alternative diagnosis established subsequently; (2) incomplete clinical data; (3) age <16 years; (4) immunocompromised status, defined as glucocorticoid or immunosuppressant use within 1 month, human immunodeficiency virus infection, solid or hematological malignancy, long-term nursing home residency, or hospitalization within 90 days; and (5) co-infection with severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2, hepatitis C virus, Brucella, Mycobacterium tuberculosis, or Treponema pallidum to avoid potential confounding.2.2Clinical data and plasma sample collectionBaseline demographic and clinical data were obtained from electronic medical records, including age, sex, comorbidities, heart rate, maximum body temperature, respiratory rate, and the interval between disease onset and ICU admission. The lowest Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) score within 24 h before ICU admission and before sedation was recorded, along with altered mental status, bleeding events, and secondary infections. The primary endpoint was 28-day mortality after ICU admission. Laboratory parameters measured within 24 h of ICU admission included viral load, lactate, and other relevant laboratory indicators. Peripheral venous blood samples were collected in the morning within 24 h after ICU admission. All enrolled patients were fasting at the time of sampling. Blood was collected in anticoagulant tubes and immediately transported to the laboratory, where the samples were centrifuged at 1, 500 × g for 15 min. The upper plasma layer was collected and stored at −80 °C until further analysis. Before analysis, plasma samples were thawed on ice at 4 °C. To ensure sample quality, all samples included in this study underwent only one freeze–thaw cycle. To minimize potential bias, the sample-processing and LC-MS/MS injection orders were randomized between the survivor and non-survivor groups.2.3Metabolite extraction and LC-MS/MS analysisAll plasma samples were thawed on ice and vortexed vigorously. Hydrophilic metabolites were extracted using pre-cooled methanol. Briefly, 100 μL of homogenized plasma was mixed with 300 μL of pre-cooled methanol, vortexed thoroughly, and incubated at −20 °C for 30 min. The supernatants were then collected for instrumental analysis. Chromatographic separation was performed using a SHIMADZU-LC30 ultra-high-performance liquid chromatography system equipped with an ACQUITY UPLC® HSS T3 column (2.1×100 mm, 1.8 μm) (Waters, Milford, MA, USA) and mass spectrometric analysis was performed using a QE Plus mass spectrometer (Thermo Fisher Scientific) with electrospray ionization in both positive and negative modes (Supplementary Information File S1). Raw mass spectrometry data were processed using MSDIAL software for peak alignment, retention-time correction, and peak-area extraction. Metabolite structures were identified by accurate-mass matching (mass tolerance <20 ppm) and MS2 spectrum matching (mass tolerance <0.01 Da) against public databases, including the Human Metabolome Database (HMDB), and a self-established in-house database. Ion peaks with >50% missing values within either group were excluded from subsequent statistical analyses. Before statistical analysis, all data were normalized to the total peak area to improve comparability and reduce variation.To monitor analytical stability, quality control (QC) samples prepared by pooling equal volumes of all plasma samples were injected after every 15 experimental samples. QC assessment included comparison of base peak chromatograms of QC samples in both positive and negative ion modes, with consistent peak intensities and retention times across injections indicating minimal instrument variation, as well as principal component analysis of QC samples, which showed tight clustering and satisfactory repeatability. Because all samples were analyzed in a single batch and QC evaluation indicated stable instrument performance, no inter-batch correction was required.2.4Proteome sample preparation and data-independent acquisition mass spectrometry data analysisSamples were thawed at 4 °C, and 2 μL of each sample was dissolved in 48 μL of UA buffer, incubated at 37 °C for 1 h, sonicated for 2 min, centrifuged, and then incubated at 4 °C for 20 min. The supernatants were collected. Low-abundance proteins were enriched using a low-abundance protein enrichment kit. An appropriate volume of 1 M DTT was added to the enriched samples to achieve a final concentration of 100 mM, followed by incubation at 37 °C for 30 min and cooling to 24 °C. Subsequently, an appropriate volume of IAA was added to achieve a final concentration of 50 mM, and the samples were incubated at room temperature for 30 min in the dark. Each sample was diluted sixfold with 50 mM NH4HCO3, after which 8 μg of Trypsin was added, and the resulting mixture was vortexed at 600 rpm for 1 min and incubated at 37 °C for 20 h. The enzymatically digested samples were acidified with an appropriate volume of TFA, and the peptides were desalted using a C18 cartridge and reconstituted in 0.1% FA; peptide concentrations were then determined before LC-MS analysis. Appropriate amounts of peptides from each sample were separated using a Vanquish Neo UHPLC system (Thermo Fisher Scientific) (Supplementary Information File S2).After peptide separation, DIA mass spectrometry was performed using an Orbitrap Astral mass spectrometer (Thermo Fisher Scientific). The total analysis duration was 8 min, with an electrospray voltage of 2.2 kV in positive-ion detection mode. The precursor-ion scan range was 380–980 m/z, the full scan resolution was 240, 000, the AGC target was 500%, and the maximum ion injection time (IT) for the full scan was 3 ms. The MS2 parameters were as follows: resolution, 80, 000; AGC target, 500%; maximum IT, 3 ms; RF lens, 40%; activation type, HCD; isolation window, 2 Th; normalized collision energy, 25%; and cycle time, 0.6 s.All mass spectrometry data were processed using DIA-NN software for database searching and quantitative analysis of the DIA mass spectrometry data. The database used was the Swiss-Prot-Homo sapiens (Human) [9606]-reviewed-20421-20250908-iRT.fasta database. Subsequently, statistical analyses were performed on the qualitative and quantitative DIA proteomic results. Each sample was prepared independently and, after enzymatic protein digestion, subjected to DIA analysis. The resulting raw DIA mass spectrometry files were imported into DIA-NN for analysis using a q value threshold of ≤0.01.2.5Omics data processing, bioinformatics, and statistical analysisProteins and metabolites with valid measurements in fewer than 50% of samples in either group were excluded from further analyses. For metabolomics, differential metabolites were identified using the OPLS-DA model with variable importance in projection (VIP) >1.0, combined with univariate analysis (P < 0.05), an approach suited to the high-dimensional and multicollinear nature of metabolomic data. Metabolites were compared between survivors and non-survivors. Based on the intensity ratio of survivors/non-survivors, up-regulated metabolites denote higher abundance in non-survivors, while down-regulated metabolites denote higher abundance in survivors. For proteomics, differentially expressed proteins were defined based on a fold-change threshold (|FC| ≥ 1.5) and P < 0.05. The FC-based criterion was adopted because proteomic datasets typically contain fewer and more directly interpretable features than metabolomic datasets, for which multivariable filtering (e.g., VIP) is more commonly applied.Correlation analysis was used to evaluate associations between the four tryptophan metabolites and plasma proteins, as well as between the metabolites and clinical parameters. To determine whether these associations were independent of intergroup differences, correlations were calculated separately in the overall cohort (n = 68) and in the survivor (n = 33) and non-survivor (n = 35) groups. Within each stratum, P values were adjusted for multiple testing using the Benjamini–Hochberg method to control the FDR. In the overall cohort, proteins with |r| ≥0.35 and P < 0.05 were considered significantly correlated with the corresponding metabolite and were eligible for inclusion in the integrated metabolite–protein network. Associations that remained significant (P < 0.05) within either subgroup were defined as robust associations.Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves were constructed to assess the discriminative value of differential metabolites and proteins for 28-day mortality in patients with severe SFTS. The area under the curve (AUC), sensitivity, specificity, and 95% confidence interval (95% CI) were calculated. Categorical variables are presented as frequencies and percentages, whereas continuous variables are expressed as medians with interquartile ranges (IQRs). Continuous variables were compared between groups using the Wilcoxon rank-sum test or Kruskal–Wallis test, whereas categorical variables were analyzed using the chi-square test or Fisher’s exact test. Multiple-testing correction was performed using the Benjamini–Hochberg method. All statistical tests were two-tailed, and P < 0.05 was considered statistically significant. All analyses were performed using R, SPSS version 19.0, MedCalc version 15.8, and MetaboAnalyst version 4.0 (Wishart Research Group, University of Alberta, Canada). (http://www.metaboanalyst.ca/). 2.1Study design and participantsThis prospective cohort study included patients with severe SFTS who were admitted to the ICU between July 2019 and October 2023. According to their 28-day clinical outcomes, patients were divided into survivor (n = 33) and non-survivor (n = 35) groups. The study was approved by the Ethics Review Committee of Yantai Qishan Hospital (approval no. 202503). The participants were informed about the research and its potential risks and provided written informed consent in accordance with the Declaration of Helsinki. The inclusion criteria (11) were as follows: (1) detection of novel bunyavirus nucleic acids in blood samples, confirmed by reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR) in the laboratory, and (2) fulfillment of the criteria for severe and critical disease classification outlined in the Consensus on Diagnosis and Treatment of Severe Fever with Thrombocytopenia Syndrome (2022 Edition). The exclusion criteria were as follows: (1) clinically suspected severe SFTS with an alternative diagnosis established subsequently; (2) incomplete clinical data; (3) age <16 years; (4) immunocompromised status, defined as glucocorticoid or immunosuppressant use within 1 month, human immunodeficiency virus infection, solid or hematological malignancy, long-term nursing home residency, or hospitalization within 90 days; and (5) co-infection with severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2, hepatitis C virus, Brucella, Mycobacterium tuberculosis, or Treponema pallidum to avoid potential confounding. 3Results3.1Participant demographics and clinical dataThe patient enrollment and exclusion process is summarized in the flow diagram (Supplementary Information Figure S1). A total of 68 patients were enrolled in this study, and the baseline characteristics were compared between the 28-day survivor (n = 33) and non-survivor (n = 35) groups. No statistically significant difference were observed between the two groups in demographic characteristics (e.g., age and sex) or most comorbidities (e.g., diabetes mellitus, hypertension, and coronary heart disease) (all P > 0.05).However, regarding clinical and laboratory parameters, patients in the non-survivor group exhibited a more severe disease phenotype, characterized by a significantly lower median GCS (9.0 vs. 11.0, P = 0.002) and a substantially higher median viral RNA copy number (1, 150, 000 vs. 8, 138, P < 0.001). Moreover, the non-survivor group showed a more pronounced systemic inflammatory response, as evidenced by significantly elevated levels of lactate, PCT, IL-6, and ferritin (all P < 0.05). Regarding organ dysfunction, this group had significantly higher levels of liver function markers (ALT, AST, and ALP), renal function parameters (BUN, Cr, and Cys-C), and myocardial injury indicators (hsTnI and BNP) (all P < 0.05). Regarding coagulation function, the non-survivor group had significantly prolonged PT, APTT, INR, and TT, along with a markedly lower FIB level and significantly elevated D-dimer levels (all P < 0.05). Blood was collected in anticoagulant tubes and immediately transported to the laboratory, where the samples were centrifuged at 1, 500 × g for 15 min. The upper plasma layer was collected and stored at −80 °C until further analysis. Before analysis, plasma samples were thawed on ice at 4 °C. Hydrophilic metabolites were extracted using pre-cooled methanol. Briefly, 100 μL of homogenized plasma was mixed with 300 μL of pre-cooled methanol, vortexed thoroughly, and incubated at −20 °C for 30 min. The supernatants were then collected for instrumental analysis. Each sample was diluted sixfold with 50 mM NH4HCO3, after which 8 μg of Trypsin was added, and the resulting mixture was vortexed at 600 rpm for 1 min and incubated at 37 °C for 20 h. full_text_sections.results: 3Results3.1Participant demographics and clinical dataThe patient enrollment and exclusion process is summarized in the flow diagram (Supplementary Information Figure S1). A total of 68 patients were enrolled in this study, and the baseline characteristics were compared between the 28-day survivor (n = 33) and non-survivor (n = 35) groups. No statistically significant difference were observed between the two groups in demographic characteristics (e.g., age and sex) or most comorbidities (e.g., diabetes mellitus, hypertension, and coronary heart disease) (all P > 0.05).However, regarding clinical and laboratory parameters, patients in the non-survivor group exhibited a more severe disease phenotype, characterized by a significantly lower median GCS (9.0 vs. 11.0, P = 0.002) and a substantially higher median viral RNA copy number (1, 150, 000 vs. 8, 138, P < 0.001). Moreover, the non-survivor group showed a more pronounced systemic inflammatory response, as evidenced by significantly elevated levels of lactate, PCT, IL-6, and ferritin (all P < 0.05). Regarding organ dysfunction, this group had significantly higher levels of liver function markers (ALT, AST, and ALP), renal function parameters (BUN, Cr, and Cys-C), and myocardial injury indicators (hsTnI and BNP) (all P < 0.05). Regarding coagulation function, the non-survivor group had significantly prolonged PT, APTT, INR, and TT, along with a markedly lower FIB level and significantly elevated D-dimer levels (all P < 0.05). full_text_sections.discussion: 4DiscussionSevere fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome (SFTS) poses a serious public health threat in East Asia, with substantially higher mortality among critically ill patients than in the general SFTS population. Clinical outcomes in severe SFTS are highly heterogeneous (1–4), reflecting complex host–virus interactions, dysregulated systemic inflammation, and progressive multi-organ dysfunction. In this context, integrated proteomic and metabolomic approaches have emerged as powerful tools for characterizing molecular changes associated with disease progression, identifying potential prognostic biomarkers, and informing the investigation of therapeutic targets in severe viral infections. Accumulating evidence supports the utility of omics strategies for investigating SFTS pathogenesis. Zhao et al. (5) demonstrated that proteomic profiling identifies dysregulated proteins involved in multiple cellular and immune processes in SFTS patients and established a proteasome-centered regulatory axis associated with adverse outcomes. Park et al. (6), by combining targeted proteomics with single-cell transcriptomics, characterized the peripheral blood immune landscape in SFTS and showed that, in fatal cases, SFTSV infection was associated with excessive inflammatory cascades involving proinflammatory cytokines and chemokines, accompanied by aberrant suppression of adaptive immunity. Zhu et al. (7) reported that serum metabolomic profiling of acute-phase SFTS patients linked perturbations in multiple metabolic pathways, particularly sphingolipid metabolism, to poor prognosis. Despite the considerable potential of multi-omics integration in severe viral infections (8–10), few studies have focused specifically on critically ill SFTS patients admitted to the intensive care unit (ICU), and the interplay between metabolic disturbances and proteomic dysregulation in fatal outcomes remains poorly characterized. This study provides the first integrated proteomic–metabolomic analysis of ICU patients with severe SFTS stratified by 28-day outcomes, aiming to characterize the metabolic and proteomic features associated with fatal disease.Consistent with previous clinical observations (11), baseline characteristics indicated a more severe disease phenotype in non-survivors, including lower Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) scores, higher SFTSV RNA loads, more pronounced systemic inflammation, multi-organ dysfunction involving the liver, kidney, and myocardium, coagulation disturbances, and reduced CD4+ and CD8+ T-lymphocyte counts. These findings further support the association of dysregulated host immune responses, systemic inflammation, and multi-organ injury with death in severe SFTS.The central finding of this study is the marked divergence in metabolite and protein profiles and signaling pathways between survivors and fatal cases. Among the perturbed pathways, tryptophan metabolism showed the strongest enrichment (hsa00380; 10/106 metabolites; adjusted P = 0.001), consistent with previous urine metabolomic findings identifying tryptophan metabolism as a major perturbed pathway in SFTS (12). As an essential amino acid, tryptophan participates in diverse physiological processes, including neuronal function, immune regulation, and intestinal homeostasis (13). In mammals, free tryptophan is predominantly catabolized via the kynurenine pathway, which is initiated by the rate-limiting enzymes IDO1 and TDO (14, 15). Our data showed significantly lower L-tryptophan (P = 0.0067) and higher levels of kynurenine and its downstream products KA, 3-HAA, XA, and 5-HIP in non-survivors (Supplementary Information Table S2). This pattern of lower substrate levels and higher product levels yields a metabolite signature consistent with enhanced kynurenine pathway activity in the setting of infection and critical illness (16–18). In COVID-19 and sepsis, elevated kynurenine-to-tryptophan ratios have been associated with disease severity and mortality (16, 18). Notably, a urine metabolomic study of SFTS likewise identified tryptophan metabolism as the top pathway distinguishing fatal from surviving patients, with elevated 5-HIAA, kynurenine, 5-HTP, and 3-HAA in fatal cases (12), supporting our findings in an independent biospecimen dimension. Importantly, our plasma-based observations suggest, but do not establish, activation of the kynurenine pathway; enzyme activities and metabolic fluxes were not directly measured, a limitation addressed below. Kynurenine pathway metabolites exert broad immunomodulatory effects: kynurenine is an endogenous ligand of the aryl hydrocarbon receptor (AhR) (19); 3-HAA modulates T-cell function and may promote an imbalance between Th17 and regulatory T cells (20, 21); and KA has been positively correlated with inflammatory cytokines and chemokines and negatively correlated with T-cell responses in severe viral infections such as COVID-19 (22). These metabolite-mediated immunomodulatory actions may contribute to immune dysregulation in fatal SFTS. Moreover, the positive correlation of 3-HAA with renal function indicators (BUN and Cys-C) suggests that impaired renal clearance may contribute to metabolite accumulation in fatal cases, a phenomenon also reported in COVID-19, where kynurenine metabolites correlate with renal status and IL-6 levels (17). Altered tryptophan metabolism may thus reflect enhanced IDO/TDO activity together with hepatic and renal dysfunction and the hyperinflammatory, hypercatabolic state of critical illness; these potential mechanisms warrant further investigation.Beyond tryptophan metabolism, purine catabolism was also associated with fatal SFTS: xanthine and uric acid were significantly higher in non-survivors (Supplementary Information Table S2), consistent with the enrichment of nucleotide metabolism. Purine catabolism can generate reactive oxygen species, and uric acid can act as a damage-associated molecular pattern to promote inflammation (23, 24). Accordingly, serum adenosine deaminase (ADA), a key enzyme in purine catabolism that catalyzes the deamination of adenosine to inosine (25), was elevated in fatal SFTS patients and correlated with IL-6, TNF-α, and multi-organ failure (26). Enhanced purine turnover has likewise been observed in COVID-19 non-survivors (27). Together with the elevated purine catabolites in non-survivors, these data support increased purine catabolism in fatal SFTS, although causal roles require functional validation.Complementing the metabolomic findings, proteomic analysis identified 200 differentially expressed proteins (DEPs) between the two groups. Proteins upregulated in survivors were predominantly enriched in proteasome and neurodegeneration-related pathways, with proteasome enrichment showing the strongest enrichment signal, consistent with Zhao et al. (5). In contrast, proteins upregulated in non-survivors were mainly associated with IL-17 signaling, TNF/NF-κB signaling, chemokine signaling, and cytokine–cytokine receptor interaction pathways, which are involved in inflammation and immune regulation, suggesting more intense inflammatory responses in fatal cases. Notably, four key proteins (SHROOM3, SEPSECS, MYH11, and PIGW) have been reported to have prognostic value (28, 29). These divergent expression profiles suggest that protein homeostasis may be relatively preserved in survivors, whereas fatal cases are characterized by greater activation of inflammatory signaling pathways. Integrative correlation analysis of the four core tryptophan metabolites with 200 DEPs identified a potential metabolite–protein association network in severe SFTS. In the overall cohort, 20 DEPs were significantly correlated with at least one core metabolite (|r| ≥ 0.35, P < 0.05), and six associations remained significant after stratification by outcome, including MMP3, SH3BGR, and BIN1, which were negatively correlated with 3-HAA in survivors, and CHL1, PLSCR3, and MYOF, which were correlated with 3-HAA/XA in non-survivors (…

First identified in China in 2009, SFTS has emerged as a major public health threat in East Asia, with endemic areas extending across China, Japan, South Korea, and Vietnam (2). Clinically, SFTS is characterized by acute high fever, marked thrombocytopenia and leukopenia, and multi-organ injury (3). Severe cases can progress rapidly to hemorrhagic diathesis, altered mental status, shock, and disseminated intravascular coagulation (4). Critically ill patients with concurrent multi-organ failure and central nervous system involvement have an extremely high mortality rate of up to 79.3%, whereas the mortality among ICU-admitted patients is approximately 44.7%, substantially exceeding the 10%–30% case-fatality rate reported in general SFTS cohorts (4). Currently, no specific antiviral agent or licensed vaccine is available, and clinical management remains largely supportive (5).In viral infectious diseases, conventional clinical indicators and pathogen-detection methods are insufficient to comprehensively characterize the complex molecular interactions between viruses and their hosts (6). In contrast, metabolomics can dynamically characterize endogenous metabolic perturbations and pathway reprogramming associated with viral replication, providing biochemical insights into organ injury and disease severity (8). papers.full_text_excerpt: This prospective cohort study enrolled 68 patients with SFTS, who were admitted to the ICU and classified them as survivors (n = 33) or non-survivors (n = 35) according to their 28-day clinical outcomes. 2Materials and methods2.1Study design and participantsThis prospective cohort study included patients with severe SFTS who were admitted to the ICU between July 2019 and October 2023. The study was approved by the Ethics Review Committee of Yantai Qishan Hospital (approval no. To ensure sample quality, all samples included in this study underwent only one freeze–thaw cycle. papers.title_original: Integrated proteomic and metabolomic profiling characterizes tryptophan metabolic disturbance associated with mortality in ICU-admitted SFTS patients

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to characterize the integrated proteomic and metabolomic mechanisms underlying mortality in ICU-admitted SFTS patients, as SFTS remains a poorly understood public health threat with high mortality rates in severe cases.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A prospective cohort study was conducted on ICU-admitted patients with severe SFTS between July 2019 and October 2023, dividing them into survivor (n = 33) and non-survivor (n = 35) groups based on 28-day clinical outcomes.
analysis.methods: Baseline demographic and clinical data were collected from electronic medical records, and laboratory parameters such as viral load, lactate, and other indicators were measured within 24 h of ICU admission. Specimens were collected in the Department of Critical Care Medicine, Yantai Qishan Hospital, and the study was approved by the Ethics Review Committee of Yantai Qishan Hospital.
analysis.main_results: No statistically significant differences were observed in demographic characteristics or most comorbidities between the survivor and non-survivor groups (all P > 0.05). However, the non-survivor group had significantly lower median GCS (9.0 vs. 11.0, P = 0.002), higher median viral RNA copy number (1,150,000 vs. 1,000,000, P < 0.05), and elevated levels of lactate, PCT, IL-6, and ferritin (all P < 0.05). Additionally, the non-survivor group showed higher levels of liver, renal, and myocardial injury markers (all P < 0.05) and prolonged coagulation parameters with reduced FIB and elevated D-dimer levels (all P < 0.05).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study identified marked disruption of tryptophan metabolism in non-survivors, with decreased L-tryptophan and increased kynurenine pathway metabolites, suggesting a potential link between metabolic disturbances and adverse outcomes in SFTS.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings may inform the development of targeted diagnostic and therapeutic strategies for SFTS, particularly in identifying metabolic biomarkers associated with mortality in critically ill patients.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study had a limited sample size and potential confounding factors, such as co-infections and immunocompromised status, which were excluded. The evidence is moderate due to these limitations and the focus on observational data.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the proteomic and metabolomic profiles of ICU-admitted SFTS patients to identify mechanisms associated with mortality. A prospective cohort design was used, with patients divided into survivor and non-survivor groups based on 28-day outcomes. The study collected clinical data and laboratory parameters, including GCS scores, viral load, and inflammatory markers. Results showed no significant differences in demographics or comorbidities but highlighted more severe clinical and laboratory features in non-survivors. Metabolomic profiling revealed significant tryptophan metabolic disturbances, with decreased L-tryptophan and increased kynurenine pathway metabolites in non-survivors. These findings suggest a potential role for metabolic biomarkers in predicting mortality in SFTS. The study's limitations include a small sample size and exclusion of certain confounding factors, resulting in moderate evidence strength.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在阐明发热伴血小板减少综合征在ICU住院的发热伴血小板减少综合征患者中整合的蛋白质组和代谢组机制,因为发热伴血小板减少综合征仍然是一个了解不足的公共卫生威胁,在严重病例中具有较高的死亡率率。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 在2019年7月至2023年10月期间,对因严重发热伴血小板减少综合征而入住ICU的患者进行了前瞻性队列研究研究,并根据28天的临床结果将他们分为幸存者(n = 33)和非幸存者(n = 35)组。
elements_zh.methods: 基线人口统计学和临床数据从电子病历中收集,病毒载量、乳酸水平和其他指标在ICU入院24小时内进行测量。样本在烟台奇山医院重症医学科采集,该研究已获得烟台奇山医院伦理审查委员会的批准。
elements_zh.main_results: 幸存者组与非幸存者组在人口统计学特征或大多数合并症方面均未观察到统计学意义上的显著差异(所有P > 0.05)。然而,非幸存者组的中位GCS显著较低(9.0 vs. 11.0,P = 0.002),中位病毒RNA拷贝数显著较高(1,150,000 vs. 1,000,000,P < 0.05),以及乳酸、PCT、IL-6和铁蛋白水平升高(所有P < 0.05)。此外,非幸存者组的肝、肾和心肌损伤标志物水平显著升高(所有P < 0.05),凝血参数延长,纤维蛋白原(FIB)水平降低,D-二聚体水平升高(所有P < 0.05)。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 本研究发现非幸存者组中色氨酸代谢显著紊乱,表现为L-色氨酸水平降低和色氨酸代谢途径代谢物水平升高,提示代谢紊乱可能与发热伴血小板减少综合征的不良预后有关。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现可能有助于为发热伴血小板减少综合征制定针对性的诊断和治疗策略,特别是在识别危重患者中与死亡率相关的代谢生物标志物方面。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究样本量有限,且可能存在一些混杂因素,如合并感染和免疫功能低下状态,这些因素已被排除。由于这些限制以及研究主要基于观察性数据,证据强度中等。

news.content: 顶部 首页 首页 晴 / 10° PNAS | 中科大/武汉病毒研究所/昆明动物研究所在大别班达病毒治疗抗体研发上取得重要进展 病毒学界 深入探索 高考信息平台 考研辅导 体验极速搜索 近日,中国科学技术大学联合中国科学院武汉病毒研究所和中国科学院昆明动物研究所合作,在国际权威期刊《美国国家科学院院刊》(PNAS)发表题为“A highly potent bispecific antibody confers complete protection against SFTSV in preclinical models”的研究论文。该研究基于两株靶向大别班达病毒Gn糖蛋白不同表位的协同中和纳米抗体,成功构建双特异性抗体N2D2-Fc-N2C1,在小鼠和雪貂模型中展现出强效保护效果,为大别班达病毒感染的防治提供了极具临床转化潜力的候选药物。 了解东亚文化 发热伴血小板减少综合征是由大别班达病毒(Dabie bandavirus,DBV,旧称发热伴血小板减少综合征病毒,SFTSV)感染引起的急性传染病,主要通过蜱虫叮咬传播,存在人传人风险,流行于中国、日本、韩国等亚洲国家。临床表现为高烧、血小板及白细胞减少、出血和多器官衰竭,病死率高达30%。2024年,WHO将DBV列为优先关注的病原体,但目前全球尚无获批的疫苗和药物,亟需有效的治疗手段。 了解东亚文化 展开剩余 60 % 该研究通过羊驼免疫和噬菌体展示技术筛选获得多株DBVGn糖蛋白特异性中和纳米抗体。其中N2C1和N2D2具有双重中和机制:既可阻断病毒吸附,又能抑制病毒膜融合过程。结构分析显示,N2C1结合于Gn糖蛋白结构域I和III的构象表位,N2D2特异性靶向结构域I。二者分别位于病毒表面糖蛋白六聚体冠部的内侧和外侧,作用于相邻Gn糖蛋白之间的关键界面,通过稳定融合前构象,抑制融合过程中的构象重排,实现高效中和。此外,二者还具有协同中和作用,基于此构建得到双特异性抗体N2D2-Fc-N2C1,其体外中和活性大幅提升。 在干扰素受体缺陷(IFNAR-/-)小鼠致死性感染模型中,N2D2-Fc-N2C1在预防性给药和治疗性给药条件下,均展现出显著优于亲本抗体的保护效力。尤为重要的是,在临床前老年雪貂模型中,N2D2-Fc-N2C1以5 mg/kg低剂量给药,或于感染后第2天延迟给药,仍可实现100%保护,显著降低体内病毒载量并明显减轻临床症状。 该研究基于纳米抗体协同中和机制,开发出针对DBV的双特异性抗体,并在雪貂模型中系统验证其保护效力。N2D2-Fc-N2C1作为单一分子,规避了抗体鸡尾酒混合制剂在生产复杂性和药代动力学一致性方面的难题,在低剂量和延迟给药下均实现完全保护,展现出显著的临床转化优势。 中国科学技术大学博士生郭晓平、中国科学院武汉病毒研究所博士生万福建、中国科学技术大学博士后李武建和中国科学院昆明动物研究所邹清翠为共同第一作者,中国科学技术大学Sandra Chiu教授、中国科学院武汉病毒研究所舒波研究员和中国科学院昆明动物研究所李明华研究员为该论文共同通讯作者。该研究得到中国科学院战略性先导科技专项、安徽省临床与转化研究项目、中国西藏自治区科技计划项目等资助。 图1 文章主要内容摘要 Free web novels for online reading. 深入探索 殡葬行业招聘 中国传媒大学 手机搜狐APP 评论 全部 还没有人评论过,快来抢首评 抢首评 推荐阅读 白衣女神演技杠杠的 浩哥吃喝玩... 2026.10.19 353.8万+ 深入探索 登录服务 订阅时事资讯 新闻 JVI|科学家在野生型HPV18中发现能够提升病毒稳定性和感染性的新型 L1蛋白 病毒学界 5天前 241 看到姆巴佩涉华不当言论原文,心被气炸了!赚着中国的钱,还在伤害我们!没良心! news.content_original: 顶部 首页 首页 晴 / 10° PNAS | 中科大/武汉病毒研究所/昆明动物研究所在大别班达病毒治疗抗体研发上取得重要进展 病毒学界 深入探索 高考信息平台 考研辅导 体验极速搜索 近日,中国科学技术大学联合中国科学院武汉病毒研究所和中国科学院昆明动物研究所合作,在国际权威期刊《美国国家科学院院刊》(PNAS)发表题为“A highly potent bispecific antibody confers complete protection against SFTSV in preclinical models”的研究论文。该研究基于两株靶向大别班达病毒Gn糖蛋白不同表位的协同中和纳米抗体,成功构建双特异性抗体N2D2-Fc-N2C1,在小鼠和雪貂模型中展现出强效保护效果,为大别班达病毒感染的防治提供了极具临床转化潜力的候选药物。 了解东亚文化 发热伴血小板减少综合征是由大别班达病毒(Dabie bandavirus,DBV,旧称发热伴血小板减少综合征病毒,SFTSV)感染引起的急性传染病,主要通过蜱虫叮咬传播,存在人传人风险,流行于中国、日本、韩国等亚洲国家。临床表现为高烧、血小板及白细胞减少、出血和多器官衰竭,病死率高达30%。2024年,WHO将DBV列为优先关注的病原体,但目前全球尚无获批的疫苗和药物,亟需有效的治疗手段。 了解东亚文化 展开剩余 60 % 该研究通过羊驼免疫和噬菌体展示技术筛选获得多株DBVGn糖蛋白特异性中和纳米抗体。其中N2C1和N2D2具有双重中和机制:既可阻断病毒吸附,又能抑制病毒膜融合过程。结构分析显示,N2C1结合于Gn糖蛋白结构域I和III的构象表位,N2D2特异性靶向结构域I。二者分别位于病毒表面糖蛋白六聚体冠部的内侧和外侧,作用于相邻Gn糖蛋白之间的关键界面,通过稳定融合前构象,抑制融合过程中的构象重排,实现高效中和。此外,二者还具有协同中和作用,基于此构建得到双特异性抗体N2D2-Fc-N2C1,其体外中和活性大幅提升。 在干扰素受体缺陷(IFNAR-/-)小鼠致死性感染模型中,N2D2-Fc-N2C1在预防性给药和治疗性给药条件下,均展现出显著优于亲本抗体的保护效力。尤为重要的是,在临床前老年雪貂模型中,N2D2-Fc-N2C1以5 mg/kg低剂量给药,或于感染后第2天延迟给药,仍可实现100%保护,显著降低体内病毒载量并明显减轻临床症状。 该研究基于纳米抗体协同中和机制,开发出针对DBV的双特异性抗体,并在雪貂模型中系统验证其保护效力。N2D2-Fc-N2C1作为单一分子,规避了抗体鸡尾酒混合制剂在生产复杂性和药代动力学一致性方面的难题,在低剂量和延迟给药下均实现完全保护,展现出显著的临床转化优势。 中国科学技术大学博士生郭晓平、中国科学院武汉病毒研究所博士生万福建、中国科学技术大学博士后李武建和中国科学院昆明动物研究所邹清翠为共同第一作者,中国科学技术大学Sandra Chiu教授、中国科学院武汉病毒研究所舒波研究员和中国科学院昆明动物研究所李明华研究员为该论文共同通讯作者。该研究得到中国科学院战略性先导科技专项、安徽省临床与转化研究项目、中国西藏自治区科技计划项目等资助。 图1 文章主要内容摘要 Free web novels for online reading. 深入探索 殡葬行业招聘 中国传媒大学 手机搜狐APP 评论 全部 还没有人评论过,快来抢首评 抢首评 推荐阅读 白衣女神演技杠杠的 浩哥吃喝玩... 2026.10.19 353.8万+ 深入探索 登录服务 订阅时事资讯 新闻 JVI|科学家在野生型HPV18中发现能够提升病毒稳定性和感染性的新型 L1蛋白 病毒学界 5天前 241 看到姆巴佩涉华不当言论原文,心被气炸了!赚着中国的钱,还在伤害我们!没良心! analysis.brief_en: Chinese researchers from the Chinese Academy of Sciences Wuhan Institute of Virology, University of Science and Technology of China, and Kunming Institute of Zoology have published a study in PNAS describing a new bispecific antibody, N2D2‐Fc‐N2C1, that fully protects mice and ferrets from severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome virus (SFTSV) in preclinical trials. The antibody, derived from two nanobodies targeting different regions of the virus’s Gn glycoprotein, neutralizes the virus by blocking attachment and fusion and acts synergistically. In IFNAR‐/‐ mouse models and a clinical‐grade aged ferret model, a low dose of 5 mg/kg given either preventively or one day after infection prevented disease and reduced viral load. The authors highlight the antibody’s advantage over conventional antibody cocktails, noting its single‐molecule format simplifies production and pharmacokinetics. While the results are promising, clinical trials are still needed to assess safety and efficacy in humans.

news.source_body_en: Chinese researchers from the Chinese Academy of Sciences Wuhan Institute of Virology, University of Science and Technology of China, and Kunming Institute of Zoology have published a study in PNAS describing a new bispecific antibody, N2D2‐Fc‐N2C1, that fully protects mice and ferrets from severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome virus (SFTSV) in preclinical trials. The antibody, derived from two nanobodies targeting different regions of the virus’s Gn glycoprotein, neutralizes the virus by blocking attachment and fusion and acts synergistically. In IFNAR‐/‐ mouse models and a clinical‐grade aged ferret model, a low dose of 5 mg/kg given either preventively or one day after infection prevented disease and reduced viral load. The authors highlight the antibody’s advantage over conventional antibody cocktails, noting its single‐molecule format simplifies production and pharmacokinetics. While the results are promising, clinical trials are still needed to assess safety and efficacy in humans.
news.content_zh: 中国科学院武汉病毒研究所、中国科学技术大学和昆明动物研究所的研究人员在《PNAS》上发表了一项研究,描述了一种新的双特异性抗体N2D2-Fc-N2C1,该抗体在临床前试验中完全保护小鼠和水貂免受发热伴血小板减少综合征病毒(SFTSV)感染。该抗体源自针对病毒Gn糖蛋白不同区域的两个纳米抗体,通过阻断病毒附着和融合来中和病毒,并具有协同作用。在IFNAR-/-小鼠模型和临床级老年水貂模型中,无论是预防性给药还是感染后一天给药,5 mg/kg的低剂量均能防止疾病发生并降低病毒载量。作者强调了该抗体相较于传统抗体鸡尾酒的优势,指出其单分子结构简化了生产及药代动力学。尽管结果令人鼓舞,但仍需进行临床试验以评估其在人体中的安全性和有效性。

news.wechat_summary_zh: 时间：未在提供的证据中报告。；地点与对象：中国(武汉、昆明)及亚洲国家(日本、韩国)；人类和动物宿主(小鼠、水貂)。；事件：确认：中国科学院武汉病毒研究所、中国科学技术大学和昆明动物研究所的研究人员报告了一种双特异性抗体(N2D2-Fc-N2C1)，该抗体在小鼠和水貂的临床前模型中提供了对SFTSV的完全保护。；影响与风险：临床前研究显示小鼠和水貂模型中100%的保护效果；病毒载量和临床症状减少；未报告人类病例或死亡人数；风险未量化。；应对与不确定性：确认了研究进展；在小鼠和水貂模型中进行了临床前测试；尚未进行人体试验；潜在的治疗候选药物；需要进一步的临床评估；来源是PNAS发表的新闻报道。

supplementary_news.content_title: PNAS | 中科大/武汉病毒研究所/昆明动物研究所在大别班达病毒治疗抗体研发上取得重要进展
supplementary_news.content: 近日, 中国科学技术大学联合 中国科学院武汉病毒研究所 和 中国科学院 昆明动物研究所 合作 ,在国际权威期刊《美国国家科学院院刊》( PNAS )发表题为 “ A highly potent bispecific antibody confers complete protection against SFTSV in preclinical models ” 的研究论文。该研究基于两株靶向 大别班达病毒 Gn 糖 蛋白不同表位的协同中和纳米抗体,成功构建双特异性抗体 N2D2-Fc-N2C1 ,在小鼠和雪貂模型中展现出强效保护效果,为 大别班达病毒 感染的防治提供了极具临床转化潜力的候选药物。 发热伴血小板减少综合征 是由 大别班达病毒( Dabie bandavirus , DBV , 旧 称 发热伴血小板减少综合征病毒, SFTSV ) 感染引起的急性传染病,主要通过蜱虫叮咬传播,存在人传人风险,流行于中国、日本、韩国等亚洲国家。临床表现为高烧 、 血小板 及 白细胞减少、出血 和 多器官衰竭,病死率高达 30% 。 2024 年, WHO 将 DBV 列为优先关注的病原体,但目前全球尚无获批的疫苗和药物,亟需有效的治疗手段。 该研究通过羊驼免疫和噬菌体展示技术筛选获得多株 DBV Gn 糖蛋白 特异性 中和 纳米抗体。 其中 N2C1 和 N2D2 具有双重中和机制:既可阻断病毒吸附,又能抑制病毒膜融合过程。结构分析显示, N2C1 结合于 Gn 糖蛋白结构域 I 和 III 的 构象表位 , N2D2 特异性靶向结构域 I 。 二者分别位于病毒表面糖蛋白六聚体冠部的内侧 和 外侧 ,作用于相邻 Gn 糖蛋白 之间的关键界面,通过稳定融合前构象, 抑制融合过程中的构象重排, 实现高效中和 。此外,二者还具有协同中和作用,基于此构 建得到双特异性抗体 N2D2-Fc-N2C1 ,其体外中和活性大幅提升 。 在干扰素受体缺陷( IFNAR -/- )小鼠致死性感染模型中, N2D2-Fc-N2C1 在预防性给药和治疗性给药条件下,均展现出显著优于亲本抗体的保护效力 。 尤为 重要的是,在临床前老年雪貂模型中, N2D2-Fc-N2C1 以 5 mg/kg 低剂量给药,或于感染后 第 2 天 延迟给药, 仍可实现 100% 保护 , 显著降低体内病毒载量并明显减轻临床症状 。 该研究基于纳米抗体协同中和机制 ,开发出 针对 DBV 的双特异性抗体,并在雪貂模型中系统验证其保护效力。 N2D2-Fc-N2C1 作为单一分子, 规避 了抗体鸡尾酒混合制剂在生产复杂性和药代动力学一致性方面的 难题 ,在低剂量和延迟给药下均实现完全保护,展现出显著的临床转化优势。 中国科学技术大学博士生 郭晓平 、 中国科学院 武汉病毒 研究 所博士生 万福建 、中国科学技术大学博士后 李武建 和 中国科学院 昆明动物研究所 邹清翠 为共同第一作者, 中国科学技术大学 Sandra Chiu 教授、 中国科学院 武汉病毒 研究 所 舒波 研究员和 中国科学院 昆明动物研究所 李明华 研究员 为该论文共同通讯作者。 该研 究得到中国科学院战略性先导科技专项、安徽省临床与转化研究项目 、中国西藏自治区科技计划项目 等资助 。 图 1 文章主要内容摘要 返回搜狐,查看更多
